cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The party report will come through me. What have you heard about the cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone dropped it over the balcony. Were you there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're permitted to establish who was there. Who else have you asked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. Your brother says he filmed you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may send me that film before approaching any further witnesses. Have you actually seen my face in it?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 controls the report, A3 licenses inquiry instead of answering, and A5 requires evidence submission while probing its contents.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 presence question becomes A3 permitted investigation; B4 alleged footage causes A5 to test whether B has seen identifying evidence.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks a timeline and B4 reports a source; A3 and A5 restrict that inquiry without making B implausibly compliant.

heightening.evidence: B4 moves from party rumor to purported footage of A, and A5 tightens control while avoiding admission.

specificity.evidence: A1 party report and B2 fallen cake establish a concrete inquiry; B4 names the brother as source rather than inventing confirmed guilt.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 permission to investigate the question just asked exposes A evasive rank, and A5 face question sharpens that behavior.
